reviews.one_line_contribution: A per-item counterfactual ground truth of which history items a long-horizon agent actually needs after a compaction boundary, used to test whether LLM summarizers preferentially keep the needed ones (the claim: they do not), whether summary-fidelity metrics carry any signal about downstream success (the claim: they do not), and whether a type-level pinning rule learned from those need labels transfers to held-out ALFWorld task types at matched tokens.
reviews.closest_prior_work: arXiv:2606.22953, 'Plans Don't Persist: Why Context Management Is Load Bearing for LLM Agents' (2026-06-22, cit 3; verified with s2cli paper). It introduces 'replay pairing' — running the same trajectory with and without an item in history — plus compression stress tests, and concludes that agent-critical information is context-resident rather than persistent. That is the proposal's Phase-1 instrument and its central adjective ('load bearing'), already published, and it appears in neither the Related Work nor the Preprint Collision Check. It does not sink the proposal outright: it masks one privileged class (the plan), scores divergence by hidden-state cosine distance rather than paired continuation success, and never measures per-family retention or need-blindness. But it removes the 'nobody has run masking as an audit on agent traces' framing, and a reviewer who knows it will read Phase 1 as replay pairing generalized from plans to all item types. Two further verified partial pre-emptions matter. (1) arXiv:2606.29251, 'When Summaries Distort Decisions: Information Fidelity in LLM-Compressed Financial Analysis' (2026-06-28; verified) already concludes that fluent, factually plausible compression alters downstream decisions and that compression must be judged by preservation of decision-relevant context rather than efficiency or factuality — i.e. the second half of this proposal's title is a published claim, only in a non-agent domain. The proposal cites it and dismisses it in six words ('financial summaries drop caveats, not agents'), which understates the threat to P3. (2) arXiv:2608.22752 Knowledge Triage (verified) already ships type-classified, type-routed retention policies, so Phase 3 is a re-derivation of an existing mechanism from better labels rather than a new mechanism. The residual novelty is the conjunction — item-granular counterfactual labels on organic traces, a need-sensitivity test across six compaction families, and a fidelity-metric horse race — which is real but thin.
reviews.strongest_objection: The estimand does not match the treatment. Load-bearing is defined by removing ONE item and holding the rest of the history fixed; compaction removes or rewrites nearly ALL of it at once. In ALFWorld in particular, history is redundant and re-acquirable: a single object-location observation can be individually maskable (the agent re-looks, or infers it from a co-occurring item) yet the same fact is lost for good when the whole pre-boundary block is replaced by a summary. Conversely, sets of items can be jointly necessary while each is individually droppable. Single-item labels are therefore a main-effects-only decomposition of an intervention with strong interference, and no step in the plan validates that they compose. This propagates: P1's 'at least 60 percent of the summarizer's loss occurs in episodes with a load-bearing drop' and P3's R_LB-beats-fidelity result both assume a superposition the design never tests, and the 'oracle pin of the counterfactual load-bearing set' is only an oracle under that same assumption. Three secondary versions compound it. (a) The masked condition inserts an '[omitted]' marker, which tells the agent something was removed and invites re-exploration; the summarizer condition does not. Labels and audit are collected under different information about the deletion, and the asymmetry cuts in the direction that inflates the measured benefit of retention. (b) Labels and outcomes come from the same episodes and the design explicitly fixes 'same seed' across conditions, so R_LB is a predictor built from the very success outcomes it is asked to predict; AUC 0.70 against a ROUGE that had no fitting opportunity is close to guaranteed by construction and is not a fair contest. (c) arXiv:2608.24569, 'When Must Becomes Maybe' (2026-08-25, verified), shows agent handoffs can retain state content while weakening its constraint on downstream action — so an entailment judge can score an item 'retained' in a summary while the item has stopped functioning, putting a ceiling on R_LB as the mediator the whole causal story rests on. Feasibility is the other exposed flank: Phase 1 alone is roughly 600 episodes x ~20 items x ~15 steps of teacher-forced passes plus 8 stochastic continuations per diverging item, per backbone, and Phases 2-3 then cross 6 families x 3 budgets x 3 boundary positions x 3 backbones x 2 benchmarks, with a 120B MoE, on one 4xA100 node, with no total episode count or GPU-hour budget stated.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Validate composition before anything is built on the labels: mask random k-subsets of pre-boundary items at several k and check that the count (or a fitted additive score) of contained load-bearing items predicts the paired success drop; report the superadditivity gap. If it is large, switch to a set-level estimate (greedy or sampled-Shapley over item groups), or restrict the claim to items whose removal is unrecoverable. 2) Replace the '[omitted]' marker with a deletion the agent cannot see — re-render the history without the item, or use a matched-length neutral filler — and report both variants as a confound check. 3) Split the rollouts: estimate need labels on seed set A and measure compaction success loss on disjoint seed set B, and cross-fit the metric comparison so R_LB and ROUGE/faithfulness are fitted and scored on the same held-out folds; otherwise P3 is definitional, not empirical. 4) Give the power calculation for P2 specifically: TOST at a 0.05 margin on R_LB minus R_nonLB, with items clustered inside episodes and a ~20 percent load-bearing base rate, needs cluster-robust SEs and many more load-bearing items than 600 episodes may yield — state the expected count and the achievable margin. 5) Separate capability loss from cost loss with a 'recoverable by re-observation' split, reporting extra steps and tokens alongside success; CWL (2606.11213) already turns on exactly this recoverability distinction, so the audit should measure it rather than fold it into success. 6) Cite and position against arXiv:2606.22953 explicitly, saying what item-granular, rollout-confirmed labels buy over replay pairing on plans, and argue against 2606.29251 rather than dismissing it as a domain aside. 7) Cut the experimental cross-product to a declared confirmatory core (one budget, one boundary position, two backbones, ALFWorld) with the rest exploratory, and publish a GPU-hour estimate.
reviews.missing_baseline: A need-conditioned (prospective) summarizer: the same backbone summarizing the same history but prompted with the goal, the open subgoals, and an explicit 'what will later steps require?' instruction, at the identical token budget. This is the one-line prompt fix any reviewer will propose the moment they read the word 'need-blind', and it is what practitioners already do; ACON's optimized guideline is a generic compression guideline, not forward-looking need conditioning, and LLM-salience pinning is a read-time pin of raw items, not a summarizer that knows the remaining task. If a need-conditioned summarizer closes most of the full-context gap at matched tokens, P2 is a fact about a bad prompt rather than about summarizers, and Phase 3's learned type rule is unnecessary. A second omitted control: 'summary plus permission to re-observe', which separates unrecoverable information loss from extra-step cost, since ALFWorld lets the agent re-look.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified full collision on the conjunction, but the check is weaker than it presents itself and it missed the paper closest to its own mechanism. All searches below ran through the literature command (s2cli, which returns Semantic Scholar and HuggingFace hits, tagged [s2]/[hf]); WebSearch and WebFetch were unavailable in this session, so I could not check section text. Queries: (1) 'counterfactual masking of history items to identify load-bearing context for agent compaction' (literature command, unrestricted) -> arXiv:2606.22953 [hf], 2607.08032 [hf] ('What to Keep, What to Forget: A Rate-Distortion View of Memory Compaction'), 2606.00408 [hf], 2606.11213 [hf], 2606.23525 [hf]. (2) 'summarizer drops information that later steps need; per-item retention audit of agent context compaction' (literature command, --recent) -> 2607.17937, 2606.23525, 2606.00408, 2605.28876 (LogDx-CI), 2602.17913 (TierMem), all [hf]; no per-item need audit. (3) 'which history items are needed later: leave-one-out ablation of agent trajectory context ALFWorld' (literature command, --recent) -> 2607.08716 [hf] 'Remember When It Matters' (names 'behavioral state decay' — decision-relevant state buried in an expanding trajectory — and proposes a proactive memory agent as mitigation, no audit), 2606.22953 [hf] again, 2606.30005 [hf]. (4) 'Constraint Pinning governance decay compaction pin critical items outside summary agent' (literature command, --recent; closest named method) -> 2606.22528 [s2] and 2608.24569 [hf], nothing else on point. (5) 'does summary faithfulness predict downstream task success compression quality metric agent' (literature command) -> 2605.25052 [hf] 'Faithfulness Metrics Don't Measure Faithfulness', 2603.17104 [hf], 2512.17920 [hf]; adjacent, no agent-trace version. (6) 'need-blind summarization: do LLM summarizers preserve decision-relevant items at higher rate than irrelevant ones' (literature command) -> 2602.00459 [hf] 'What Matters to an LLM?' plus generic summarization work; the specific need-sensitivity test appears unpublished. arXiv IDs verified with s2cli paper: 2606.22528, 2608.22752, 2510.00615, 2603.04257, 2606.11213, 2605.23296, 2606.23525, 2607.05378, 2606.00408, 2606.29251, plus the two threats 2606.22953 and 2608.24569 — all twelve resolved and matched their stated descriptions; none failed to verify. Judgment on the proposal's own check: it is unusually detailed for this stage (six queries, IDs, per-paper differentiating statements, and it correctly verified 2608.22752 as Aug 2026), and I confirm its characterizations of 2606.22528, 2608.22752, 2510.00615 and 2606.11213. But it reports an s2cli query containing the exact phrase 'load-bearing context compaction agent' returning only 2606.00408 and 2606.11213, while my near-identical query returned arXiv:2606.22953 — titled 'Why Context Management Is Load Bearing for LLM Agents' — in the top five. Missing the one preprint that shares both the instrument (masked replay pairing with and without an item in history) and the central term turns a novelty claim into an unchecked one, and is the most damaging thing in the submission. Separately, the check reports 2606.29251 and waves it off as 'financial summaries drop caveats, not agents'; its verified abstract makes the general claim that fluent, factually plausible LLM compression alters downstream decisions and must be evaluated on decision-relevant preservation rather than factuality — the proposal's own fidelity thesis, published two months earlier in another domain. Net: no collision on the counterfactual need audit itself; verified partial pre-emption of the instrument (2606.22953), of the fidelity claim (2606.29251), and of the constructive type-routing fix (2608.22752).
